ErrorBody.description:
An error. `message` is the template of `code` with the values of `context` in its `{placeholders}`, so that a client can write it in another language from `code` and `context` alone. The codes, their status and their template:
- `IDENTIFIER_EMPTY` (400): the {parameter} must not be empty
- `IDENTIFIER_TOO_LONG` (400): the {parameter} `{value}` is longer than {maxLength} bytes
- `IDENTIFIER_INVALID_CHARACTER` (400): the {parameter} `{value}` may only contain letters, digits, `-` and `_`
- `BODY_UNREADABLE` (400): the request body could not be read
- `BODY_TOO_LARGE` (413): the request body is too large
- `BODY_NOT_JSON` (400): the request body is not valid JSON (line {line}, column {column})
- `BODY_UNKNOWN_FIELD` (400): the request body has an unknown field `{field}` (line {line}, column {column})
- `BODY_MISSING_FIELD` (400): the request body lacks the field `{field}` (line {line}, column {column})
- `BODY_INVALID` (400): the request body is invalid: {detail} (line {line}, column {column})
- `LIMIT_INVALID` (400): invalid limit `{value}`: expected a number of rows
- `QUERY_INVALID` (400): the query string is invalid: {detail}
- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` (404): unknown tenant `{tenant}`
- `TENANT_DISPLAY_NAME_CONFLICT` (409): tenant `{tenant}` already exists with another display name
- `DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG` (400): the display name is longer than {maxLength} characters
- `DISPLAY_NAME_INVALID_CHARACTER` (400): the display name contains a control character
- `GRAPH_NOT_FOUND` (404): unknown graph `{tenant}/{graph}`
- `NODE_NOT_FOUND` (404): unknown node `{node}` in graph `{tenant}/{graph}`
- `GRAPH_BEING_DELETED` (400): graph `{tenant}/{graph}` is being deleted
- `GRAPH_DECLARED_BY_CODE` (409): graph `{tenant}/{graph}` is declared by the code of the application: remove it from the code to delete it
- `GRAPH_NOT_IN_CODE` (409): graph `{tenant}/{graph}` is no longer declared by the code of the application: it can only be deleted
- `NODE_CONFIG_NOT_OBJECT` (400): the configuration of node `{node}` in graph `{tenant}/{graph}` is not an object and cannot be patched
- `NODE_FIELD_NOT_EXPOSED` (400): node `{node}` in graph `{tenant}/{graph}` does not expose the configuration field `{field}`
- `GRAPH_EMPTY` (400): the graph has no node
- `NODE_DUPLICATED` (400): node `{node}` is declared twice
- `EDGE_UNKNOWN_NODE` (400): edge `{from}` -> `{to}` references unknown node `{unknown}`
- `EDGE_INVALID` (400): edge `{from}` -> `{to}` is duplicated or a self-loop
- `GRAPH_CYCLE` (400): the graph has a cycle through {nodes}
- `OPERATOR_UNKNOWN` (400): node `{node}` references unknown operator `{op}`
- `TYPE_MISMATCH` (400): edge `{from}` -> `{to}`: `{from}` produces `{produced}` but `{to}` expects `{expected}`
- `WIRING_SOURCE_HAS_INPUTS` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): a source cannot have inputs
- `WIRING_SOURCE_WITHOUT_OUTPUTS` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): a source needs at least one output
- `WIRING_SINK_WITHOUT_INPUTS` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): a sink needs at least one input
- `WIRING_SINK_HAS_OUTPUTS` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): a sink cannot have outputs
- `WIRING_NEEDS_INPUT_AND_OUTPUT` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): needs at least one input and one output
- `WIRING_KEY_BY_MUST_FEED_WINDOWS` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): a key_by node must feed window nodes only
- `WIRING_WINDOW_MUST_BE_FED_BY_KEY_BY` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): a window node must be fed by key_by nodes only
- `WIRING_WINDOW_MUST_FEED_AGGREGATES` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): a window node must feed aggregate nodes only
- `WIRING_AGGREGATE_NEEDS_ONE_WINDOW` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): an aggregate node needs exactly one input, a window node
- `WIRING_AGGREGATE_WITHOUT_OUTPUTS` (400): node `{node}` ({kind}): an aggregate node needs at least one output
- `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE` (413): the document is {size} bytes, above the store's limit of {limit}
- `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` (503): the store did not answer, try again later
- `STORE_DOCUMENT_UNREADABLE` (503): a document of the store is unreadable
- `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` (404): nothing is served at `{path}`
- `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` (405): `{path}` does not take the method {method}, only {allowed}
- `UI_NOT_EMBEDDED` (404): the web UI is not embedded in this build

code.description: The case, a constant for machines.

context.description: The values the message is about, by placeholder name.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person, in English.

bottleneck.description: What limits the graph, if anything.

orphan.description:
Whether the code of the workers no longer declares the graph: it is
stopped, and can only be deleted.

watermarkMs.description: Minimum watermark of the source slices; null if any is unknown.

GraphId.description: A graph id: 1 to 128 letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

GraphPlan.description: How a graph is cut into slices, computed by the controller.

closed.description:
Retired slices whose state has been deleted. Their log stays closed
to the plans of that time.

closing.description:
Retired slices whose log has been closed, everything they committed
being emitted, with the instant it was: their state is deleted once
no write issued before that can still land.

error.description: Why the graph cannot be planned (unknown operator, unreachable source, ...).

generation.description:
Incremented every time the set of slices changes, as when a source
gains or loses partitions. Slice instances and commit records carry
it: nothing is written under a plan older than what the log holds.

joined.description:
Slices that entered the plan after the graph had started, with the
generation at which they did: the pipeline may have emitted windows
without them, which they must then take for closed.

partitions.description: Partition count of every source node.

retired.description:
Slices that are no longer run, their partition being gone, but whose
committed state still has to be emitted.

specVersion.description: Version of the description this plan was computed from.

GraphSettings.description: Engine settings of a graph. Every field has a default.

chunkSize.description: Number of records per chunk on an edge.

flushInterval.description: How often closed windows are looked for.

gcGrace.description:
How long the index entry of an emitted window outlives its state. A
store command issued by a worker that has since lost its slice may
still land: the entry is what lets such a write be found and deleted.
Must exceed three times the command timeout of the store, plus the
clock difference between workers.

idleTimeout.description:
After this long without any record on a fully-read partition, its
watermark follows the wall clock so that downstream windows can close.

linger.description: Maximum time a source waits to fill a batch.

mailboxCapacity.description:
Capacity of every edge, in chunks. A full edge blocks its producer:
this is what propagates backpressure up to the source.

maxBatch.description: Maximum number of source records per epoch (one KV commit per epoch).

maxInFlightEpochs.description: How many epochs a slice may have read but not yet committed.

maxOutOfOrderness.description: Watermark = highest event time seen minus this bound.

maxPendingWindows.description:
How many windows a slice may have closed, per aggregate, without their
results being emitted yet. Past that number the slice stops reading
until emission catches up: this is how a slow sink behind an aggregate
slows the sources down, and what bounds the state waiting in the store.
`0` removes the limit.

watermarkMs.description: Minimum watermark of the source slices.

backpressured.description: Share of the last interval spent waiting for room downstream.

busy.description: Share of the last interval spent working.

idle.description: Share of the last interval spent waiting for input.

inPerSec.description: Input rate over the last interval, in records per second.

lateDropped.description: Records dropped because their window was already closed.

queueLen.description: Chunks waiting in the actor's input edges.

waiting.description:
Part of `busy` spent waiting for an external system to answer (a
sink's destination), as opposed to computing. An actor that is busy
mostly waiting is limited by that system, not by this worker: more
CPU does not help it.

Limit.description: Rows to return at most (200 by default); above 2000, 2000.

Load.description: Resource usage of a worker process. Ratios are in `0.0..=1.0`.

memory.description: Memory usage of the process, relative to its limit.

NodeId.description: A node id: 1 to 128 letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

oneOf.description: At least one instance is starting.
At least one instance is paused.

backpressured.description: Backpressure ratio of the hot instance.

bottleneck.description: This node is the graph's bottleneck.

The parameters of its configuration, for tools that build graphs.
Empty when the operator takes none, or does not say.

computedBy.description: The worker that computed this placement.

Position.description: A position inside a source partition, `a.b.c`: three 64-bit integers, as text so that JavaScript does not round them.

RunState.description: Run state requested for a graph.

oneOf.description: Sources stop reading; state and positions are kept.
Sources stop reading, what is in flight is committed, then slices stop.

assignedTo.description: Worker the placement assigns the slice to.

commits.description: Commits since the slice started on this worker.

fenced.description: Times this worker lost a commit to another worker.

inFlightEpochs.description: Epochs read but not yet committed.

restarts.description: Times the slice restarted on this worker.

throttled.description:
Times this instance held back reading because too many closed windows

window.description:

worker.description: Reporting worker; null for a slice nobody reports yet.

A tenant, as created through the API. Field `<tenant>` of

displayName.description: Name shown to people, when one was given.

actors.description: Actors of the tenant on alive workers.

createdMs.description:
When the tenant was created; absent for a tenant that has graphs but
was never created (written before tenants had to be).

displayName.description: Name shown to people, when one was given.

graphs.description: Graphs in the index (including those being deleted).

inPerSec.description: Input rate of the tenant on alive workers, records per second.

TenantUsage.description: What one tenant consumes on one worker.

actors.description: Actors of the tenant running on the worker.

busy.description:
Sum of the busy ratios of its actors. Busy time includes waiting on
I/O (a sink write, a KV command), so this is occupation, not CPU.

inPerSec.description: Records its source actors read over the last interval, per second.

patch.description:
Graphs are built by the code of the workers; only the fields an operator
lists among its parameters can be changed here. Each field of the body is
laid over the configuration the code gave the node, `null` going back to
the code's value. The new description is validated and stored as a new
version, on which the node's instances restart. The fields are kept apart
from the description, so that a new version of the code keeps them.
